subject: SLA measurement, maintenance windows & credit mechanics - QuasarCloud

Subject: SLA redlines: measurement and maintenance windows

Hi Marissa / Karthik,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Attached is QuasarCloud's consolidated SLA redline packet — focused on how availability will be measured (aggregation windows), the frequency/length of maintenance windows, and the service credit mechanics. We highlighted three areas that need quick alignment so procurement can move to an internal approval: 1) measurement window (monthly vs rolling 30-day), 2) planned maintenance cadence (weekly windows vs monthly bundled windows), and 3) cap on credits (we prefer a fixed cap and an escrow-like remedy).

Specific asks:
- Can you confirm Redwood's baseline for monthly uptime calculation?
- What's the proposed notification lead-time for planned maintenance >30 minutes?
- Are there any constraints on emergency/patch windows (i.e., number of emergency patches per quarter without credit exposure)?

I've attached Quasar_SLA_Redlines_v1.pdf. Dani

--

Subject: Re: SLA redlines: measurement and maintenance windows

Hi Danielle — thanks for the packet and clear callouts. We reviewed your redlines and sketched an initial response (attached). High level: Redwood agrees on a clear, auditable measurement approach but we want a rolling 30-day calculation for uptime (it better reflects seasonal usage spikes and is standard for our hosted customers). For maintenance, we prefer a monthly scheduled maintenance window with weekly emergency patch slots limited to one per quarter without credit exposure.

Proposed quick positions:
- Availability metric: Monthly rolling 30-day uptime, measured at the control plane and edge egress, with per-region aggregation (rollup required for global accounts).
- Target: 99.97% monthly uptime for production endpoints (we can layer 99.99% for premium dedicated pools).
- Planned maintenance: 2 hours / month in a single maintenance window; 7-day advance notice for anything >30 minutes.
- Emergency patches: Allow 1 emergency patch window / quarter (<= 60 minutes) without credit. Additional emergency maintenance that impacts uptime >30 mins triggers pro-rata credits.
- Credit cap: proposed 7.5% of monthly invoice for cumulative credits (we put higher than 5% to reflect multi-region, multi-cluster accounts).

I've attached Redwood_SLA_response_20261130.pdf with language suggestions. Can we do a 30-minute sync tomorrow to walk through the escape hatches? I'm flexible after 11:00 PT.

Thanks,

Marissa / Danielle — looping in legal comments inline. Attaching an annotated MSA with recommended phrasing to (a) tighten measurement definitions, (b) limit credit exposure, and (c) establish notice and documentation requirements for planned and emergency maintenance. Summary of suggested legal positions:

1) Measurement and evidence: uptime measured over a rolling 30-day window with Redwood to provide monthly measurement reports and raw telemetry on request (redacted for customer PII). Quasar can request an audit with 30 days' notice; audit scope and cost responsibility TBD.

2) Maintenance windows and notification: Planned maintenance that could affect availability must have >=7 business days' notice if expected impact >30 minutes. For planned maintenance <=30 minutes, 48-hour notice acceptable. For emergency maintenance, Redwood will provide post-event summary within 48 hours.

3) Response times (incident tiers):
- P0 / P1 (service down): initial acknowledgement within 15 minutes, next update within 60 minutes, remediation SLA target 4 business hours for hosted tiers, faster targets for Dedicated.
- P2: acknowledgement within 1 hour, targeted remediation 24 hours.

4) Credit mechanics: A single-incident credit schedule with escalator percentages depending on downtime minutes; cumulative cap at 7.5% of monthly invoice. Credits are exclusive remedy for availability, except where mandatory law requires otherwise.

5) Change control: major upgrades impacting application-level compatibility require a canary rollout, 14-day notice, and the ability for Quasar to opt-out of scheduled change for sensitive windows.

See attached MSA_annotated_redlines.docx for redline snippets. I'm available for a legal sync if Quasar's counsel wants to walk through wording.

-Lauren

Subject: Re: SLA redlines: measurement and maintenance windows

Marissa / Lauren — appreciate the quick turnaround and detailed positions. A few items Quasar can't accept as written:

- Measurement: Quasar prefers an end-of-month monthly aggregation (calendar month) rather than rolling 30-day. The calendar month aligns with our internal billing and monitoring.
- Target: We are asking for 99.99% for production endpoints; 99.97% is lower than our requirement for customer-facing APIs.
- Maintenance cadence: Quasar's ops team strongly prefers a single monthly window (2 hours) rather than any weekly/quarterly emergency allowance that could happen more than once per quarter.
- Credit cap: our legal asks for a 5% cap; 7.5% is high for an initial term.

Also, can you provide an example operational runbook or the post-mortem template you use for emergency maintenance? That will help our SREs validate the post-event commitments. Attached is a short comment sheet (Quasar_SLA_comment_sheet.xlsx) with inline cells.

Happy to jump on the call — can you do 09:30 PT today? Danielle

--
Danielle Park

Subject: Re: SLA redlines: measurement and maintenance windows

Thanks Danielle — quick notes and a proposed compromise ahead of the 09:30 PT sync: (I will open the Zoom invite for 09:30 PT and include SRE + legal from our side)

Proposed compromise (to unblock procurement):
- Measurement: move to calendar-month aggregation for this contract term but include a 90-day review clause to evaluate switching to rolling 30-day if either party requests it.
- Target: agree to 99.97% for hosted production endpoints for the initial 12-month term, with a performance-based upgrade path to 99.99% if usage patterns meet the dedicated thresholds; alternatively, we can offer 99.99% on a Dedicated pool as an add-on.
- Maintenance: single 2-hour monthly maintenance window (we propose 03:00-05:00 UTC) with 7-day notice for events >30 minutes. Emergency patches limited to 1 per quarter without credit; additional emergency maintenance that causes downtime will trigger credits.
- Credit cap: move to 7.5% for first 6 months then step down to 5% if both parties agree after the first renewal — or we can accept a hard 5% cap if Quasar takes the Dedicated option in scope for the primary endpoints.
- Response P1: we'll target acknowledgement within 15 minutes and initial remediation updates within 60 minutes; remediation target depends on tier and environment (we will capture this in the runbook).

Action items:
- Marissa: share Redwood's post-mortem/runbook template (attached to this thread) and the annotated response PDF.
- Lauren: prepare redline snippet for the 90-day measurement-review clause and the credit-stepdown language.
- Quasar: confirm whether calendar-month aggregation is a hard requirement or negotiable and whether Dedicated pool interest is on the table.

I'll follow with the Zoom link and a DocuSign placeholder for the agreed redlines so procurement can track signatures. Looking forward to the call.

Best,
